'''Ian Keith Affleck''' (July 2, 1952 – October 4, 2024) was a Canadian physicist specializing in [[condensed matter physics]]. He was Killam University Professor, Department of Physics and Astronomy, [[University of British Columbia]].

==Life and career==
Ian Affleck was born in [[Vancouver, British Columbia]] on July 2, 1952.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ian Keith Affleck|url=http://www.science.ca/scientists/scientistprofile.php?pID=24&pg=3|access-date=29 September 2012}}</ref> He studied theoretical aspects of condensed matter physics, including [[high temperature superconductivity]], low dimensional magnetism, [[quantum dots]] and [[quantum wires]].<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.phas.ubc.ca/~iaffleck/|title = Ian Affleck|publisher = University of British Columbia, Department of Physics and Astronomy|access-date = 11 March 2014|archive-date = 12 March 2014|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140312213109/http://www.phas.ubc.ca/~iaffleck/|url-status = dead}}</ref>

Affleck made many important contributions to theoretical and mathematical physics.<ref>{{cite web|url = http://royalsociety.org/people/ian-affleck/|title=Professor Ian Affleck FRS|publisher= The Royal Society|access-date = 11 March 2014}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=In Memoriam: Ian Affleck (1952-2024) {{!}} UBC Physics & Astronomy |url=https://phas.ubc.ca/memoriam-ian-affleck-1952-2024 |access-date=2024-10-09 |website=phas.ubc.ca |language=en}}</ref> He began his career in [[high-energy physics|high energy theory]] (HEP), and has successfully applied many techniques from HEP to condensed matter. In particular, he has applied conformal field theory techniques to low dimensional magnetism, [[Kondo effects]] and quantum impurity problems. In doing so, he enjoyed finding "[[mathematically elegant]] solutions" to problems.<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Affleck&first_nm=Ian&year=2012|title= 2012 Lars Onsager Prize Recipient|publisher= American Physical Society Sites|access-date = 11 March 2014}}</ref>
He was also a member of the [[CIFAR]]'s Superconductivity Program and the Cosmology and Gravity Program.<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.cifar.ca/ian-affleck-qmt|title = Ian Affleck|publisher = CIFAR Canadian Institute for advanced Research|access-date = 11 March 2014|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140312211908/http://www.cifar.ca/ian-affleck-qmt|archive-date = 12 March 2014|url-status = dead}}</ref>

Affleck held numerous awards including the 2006 CAP Medal for Lifetime Achievement and the 2014 DCMMP Brockhouse Medal.<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.phas.ubc.ca/faculty-and-staff-awards|title= New Fellows 2010|publisher= Royal Society|access-date = 30 July 2013}}</ref>
He was elected a  [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]] in 2002 <ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2002&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive|publisher=APS|access-date=17 September 2020}} </ref> and a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url = http://royalsociety.org/about-us/fellowship/new-fellows-2010/|title= New Fellows 2010|publisher= Royal Society|access-date = 30 July 2013}}</ref>

Affleck died on October 4, 2024, at the age of 72.<ref>{{cite web |title=In Memoriam: Ian Affleck (1952–2024) |url=https://phas.ubc.ca/memoriam-ian-affleck-1952-2024 |website=The University of British Columbia |access-date=10 October 2024 |date=8 October 2024}}</ref>
